# Can an agent implement a method from its paper?

> A pre-registered benchmark of retrieval conditions for code-implementation
> agents. Four arms, identical prompt and budgets, identical held-out referee,
> varying only what retrieval the agent is given. Four runs, each against a
> pre-registration committed before any subject token was spent. Apache-2.0.

This file is the machine-oriented map. `README.md` is the human one and carries
the caveats; nothing below replaces them.

## Read this before quoting any number

- The **headline is a null result about the authors' own product**: a flat
  BM25 + cosine index over 118,400 code samples matched the knowledge-graph arm
  on every task (0 discordant pairs in 24, sign test p = 1.00). With the answer
  held out, neither arm beat having no tools at all (24/48 · 24/48 · 23/48;
  95% CI on graph-vs-flat [-11.5%, +15.6%]).
- **A tie is not equivalence.** v1.5 is a ceiling tie at 100%; the rule of
  three bounds the graph's per-task advantage at 3 in 24, not at zero.
- **`passed` is not correctness.** The referee is an LLM-drafted property
  suite. No implementation here carries a correctness claim, and none is the
  paper authors' code. An audit of the population they came from brackets
  fidelity at **0.29–0.80** with no adjudicator earning the right to narrow it.
- **`verification_level` / `served_level` mean "what execution checks it
  passed"**, never "this is the paper's method". The audit's sharpest finding
  is that the V0–V3 ladder buys no fidelity, because no rung of it reads the
  paper.
- Full list of what is not claimed: `README.md`, section "What is NOT claimed"
  (seven numbered items). Quoting a table without them is a misquote.

## Machine-readable contracts

- `schemas/artifacts.schema.json` — JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) for the four
  published shapes: `#/$defs/task`, `#/$defs/run_meta`, `#/$defs/result_row`,
  `#/$defs/manifest`. Validated against every shipped artifact on every push by
  `tools/validate_schemas.py`, so it is a checked contract, not documentation.
- `MANIFEST.json` — every file in the repository with its sha256, byte count,
  origin, and the rule that put it there (`verbatim`, `portability-patched`,
  `redacted-transcript`, `authored`, …). Verify a clone against it with
  `python3 tools/check_clean_clone.py`.
- `referees/INDEX.json` — the 72 tasks, their papers, and what each referee
  file is.
- `data/results*.json` — one referee verdict per run, per version.
  `data/runs/<sweep>/<task_id>/<arm>/meta.json` — that run's structure.
  `transcript.json` beside it — the same run, **redacted**: message order, tool
  calls and structural result fields kept, every retrieved body replaced by
  `<redacted body sha256=… bytes=… field=… origin=…>`.

## Runs with no credentials, offline, $0

```
python3 tools/smoke_referee.py            # the referee really runs here
python3 tools/verify_claims.py            # 77 checks: re-derives the tables
python3 tools/recompute_fidelity_bracket.py   # the 0.29-0.80 bracket
python3 tools/check_clean_clone.py        # compiles, imports, deps, manifest
python3 tools/scan_secrets.py             # the publication gate
python3 tools/redact_transcripts.py --verify
python3 src/qc/qc_code_only_arm.py        # exits 4: C and D need an index
```

Exit codes, everywhere in this project: `0` clean, `1` findings, `2` drift,
`3` unaccepted exclusions, `4` unresolved partials. **An exit 3 or 4 is the
tool refusing to claim completeness**, not a crash.

## Needs credentials, or cannot be run at all

- `none` arm — AWS Bedrock. ~$0.056 per task. The floor every arm is measured
  against, and it is high: 13/24 in the freeze.
- `search` arm — plus a GitHub token and a Semantic Scholar key. Its toolkit
  drifted after the freeze; the freeze is its last clean measurement.
- `code_only` arm — needs a flat index you build **and** a Neo4j store. Ours is
  not published: 71.0% of its harvested rows carry no redistributable licence.
- `syntology` / `syntology_ho` arms — **not runnable by anyone outside
  Syntology.** Private graph, unpublished serving code.
- `src/analyze_substitution.py` — needs a graph, at all.
- `tools/assemble.py` — needs the working repo. Refuses with exit 2.

So the headline comparison is **re-derivable from `data/`, not re-runnable**.
`CONTRIBUTING.md` says that plainly and says why.

## Files

- `README.md` — the claims, and what is not claimed.
- `REPRODUCTION.md` — what you can and cannot reproduce; every command in it
  was executed from a clean clone before it was written.
- `prereg/` — the pre-registrations, verbatim, as committed before each run.
- `results/` — the results documents, with predictions scored.
- `ASSEMBLY_REPORT.md` — what was scanned, found, excluded, and what is still
  not right (§4 and §6 are the honest list).
- `LICENSE_QUESTION.md` — the licence decision and the two things it does not
  settle. `NOTICE` — what the grant covers and what it cannot.
- `CONTRIBUTING.md` · `SECURITY.md` — scope, and the fact that this repository
  ships generated code that the referee executes on your machine.
- `CITATION.cff` — machine-readable citation. No DOI yet.

## Read this before quoting any number from the benchmark tables
- GRAPH_STATE.md — the v1.5/v1.6 runs were scored while the graph was being
  written to: 90 overlapping writes (39 changing node/edge counts, 51 property
  writes), re-derivable from data/run_window_ledger.json. Those results are
  NOT re-tested against the current graph.
- Method has grown 63% since that run. An author measurement; not checkable here.
- FREEZE_RUN separation (graph 21/24 vs search 11/24) and the v1.5/v1.6 null
  are DIFFERENT runs. Read both before quoting either.
